steps.title: Welcome to Dossiq
steps.body: In seven steps you register your first case and see where it goes. The case you save is a real record, not a demo.
You work from this list: every case in the organisation, open and closed.
Register your first case. Give it a title, pick a case type, then save. You can add tasks, decisions and documents later.

steps.title: Where case types come from
steps.body: Every case follows a case type, its blueprint. The case type decides the statuses a case moves through, how long it may take, who handles it and what may be decided. Have a look; you do not need to make one, 88 ship with the app.

steps.title: Where the automation lives
steps.body: Flows are what happens without anyone clicking: a deadline that warns before it passes, a confirmation that goes out on submission. This is where you read and edit them. Nothing to build now.
Your work lives here: today's tasks, deadlines and open cases in one place.

Was three of the eleven widgets on the combined Dashboard page; split out because the Dashboard answers "how is the team doing" while this answers "what do I do first today", and a handler opening the app wants the second question, not the first. `slots.widget-my-work` moved here for the same reason `_note` on the old Dashboard page warned about: a `type: "custom"` widget resolves ONLY through the page's own top-level `slots` map, never through one nested under `config`.

widgets.title: My work
widgets._note: remove-casetask 2.3. This tile read `register: dossiq, schema: caseTask`, a store nothing writes any more. The read answered 200, so the page rendered a table of rows no writer had touched since the engine took over, and it would have gone empty the day that schema is deleted. It now reads OpenRegister's task engine through `useEngineTaskStore`, the seam every other task surface in dossiq already reads. TYPE is the interim. `type: "custom"` resolves through the page slot `widget-my-work` in this page's `slots` map, because [blocked: nextcloud-vue 2.46.0 ships a `tasks` entity source for INDEX pages only, `src/composables/indexSources.js`, and no widget equivalent], so no manifest key can name this list. TARGET: back to a generic widget the day the library grows a task source for widgets, at which point `src/views/widgets/MyWorkWidget.vue` and its registry entry are deleted. `limit`, `rowRoute`, `viewAllRoute`, `viewAllLabel` and `emptyText` are kept as written and the component reads every one of them, so the swap back is a retype and not a rewrite. `viewAllRoute` CARRIES NO QUERY, and it used to carry `assignee: @me` plus `isTerminalStatus: false`. remove-casetask 2.2 moved the Tasks index onto `entitySource: "tasks"`, and a named source reads NOTHING from the route: `useNamedSource.loadActive()` merges the page's `sourceConfig` with the active quick-filter tab and never looks at `$route.query`, and CnIndexPage's `$route.query` watcher is guarded on `isSelfFetchMode`, which a named source is not. The old query therefore did not narrow the list, it was simply ignored, and a query left in place would claim a filter the page does not apply. View all lands on the index's default All tab; the reader's own tab is Mine, one chip away. It comes back the day a named source grows the `?key=value` grammar `resolveQueryFilters` already gives a self-fetching one. The Case column is NOT kept: the engine answers the case in its `subject` block, that block came back null on all fifty rows the live instance returned on 2026-09-10, and a column blank on every row is the same looks-fine-shows-nothing failure this widget is being fixed for. The cause is in OpenRegister's TaskInboxService, which takes its object mapper as an optional constructor argument and gets null.

content.emptyText: You have no open tasks

widgets.title: Deadlines
widgets._note: openspec/changes/dashboard-tiles design D1. Replaces `overdue-cases` and `deadline-alerts`, which read `case` with the same `isFinalStatus: false` filter and differed only in the deadline window, so seven of nine rows appeared twice. One window now covers both: everything already past its deadline and everything due within three days, ordered by deadline. The red row is `rowClass`, not the `cn-cell--danger` the design sketched: a column's `cellClass` is one static string, so it cannot carry a per-branch colour, and the spec asks for the ROW to read in the error colour anyway.

content._viewAllNote: one-case-list A22, triage item 4. The query is this table's OWN filter in the flat bracket grammar, key for key, and `dashboardViewAllRoutes.spec.js` holds that invariant for every tile: a table that counts one set of cases and a View all that lands on another is the dropped filter this fixes. The nested `{ deadline: { lte } }` form belongs in a `source.filter`, which the widget reads, and NOT in a route query, which `buildQueryString` would JSON-stringify into a literal object string that matches nothing. Note the WINDOW: this table is overdue AND due within three days, wider than the Cases page's Overdue chip, so it deliberately does not carry that chip's filter. `kpi-overdue` is the widget whose count the Overdue chip reproduces exactly, and that equality is asserted. CnIndexPage merges the query into the fetch under the page's own filter, so the filter arrives and the list is right; what it does NOT do is activate a matching chip, because `resolveInitialQuickFilterIndex` reads only `default`. The reader lands on All with the query applied and no chip showing why, and naming a chip from a query needs a nextcloud-vue change.

pages.title: Queue
pages._note: The one queue: every case that is open and that nobody has picked up. It is a FILTER over `case`, not a collection of its own, so this is a plain type:index rather than a bespoke view. `assignee: "IS NULL"` is the literal sentinel every OpenRegister condition builder matches by value. The suffix spelling `assignee_isnull=true` was dead when this page shipped: the only code that mentioned it had no callers, and `isnull` was missing from MagicSearchHandler::COMPARISON_OPERATORS, so the filter contributed no condition at all. Fixed in openregister `isnull-filter-operator`; the sentinel is kept because it also works on instances that do not yet carry that change. `isFinalStatus: false` keeps closed cases out; it is a real boolean on every case row, not a derived one, so plain equality reaches it. Assigning a case removes it from here and puts it on that person's Assigned to me; All cases shows it either way. The caseType folder sidebar is the same control the Cases index uses, so the queue narrows by case type without a second page. WHY THIS IS A PAGE AND NOT A `menu[].query` PRESET, which is what gate-68 (ADR-097 Decision 5) proposes for a second index over an already-indexed schema: a preset is only a link into the target page, where the query filters and the reader's own facet filters share one map, so a facet interaction can widen the queue back to every case. A base filter on the page itself cannot be cleared by the person reading it, and that is the property that makes the queue trustworthy. Assigned to me is a page for the same reason.

config.emptyText: Nothing is waiting. Every open case has someone on it.

pages.title: My Work
pages._note: Case index scoped to the current user (assignee = current uid) in card view. A thin CnIndexPage wrapper because the stock index base-filter does not resolve the @me current-user token; the wrapper injects the resolved uid.

pages.title: Cases
pages._note: `excludeFields: [status]` keeps the status picker OFF this page's form dialog, and the reason is not cosmetic. On CREATE the picker listed every case type's statuses. CnFormDialog loads a reference field's options once, at open time, and `status` carries `x-relation-filter: { caseType: "@object.caseType" }`: a token that resolves to nothing while the form is still empty, so the fetch goes out unfiltered and never goes out again. Half those options are named `Received` or `In progress`, belong to a different case type, and are therefore both indistinguishable and wrong. A case is born with its own case type's `initialStatus` through `x-openregister-prefill`, so there is no status a person should be picking here at all. On EDIT the token does resolve and the picker is correctly scoped, but a raw dropdown writes the field straight through: no statusRecord, no guard evaluation, none of the transition's `automaticActions`. A status is the OUTPUT of a transition, not a field. CaseDetail's `lifecycleActions.field: status` is where one changes.

config._bulkActionsNote: one-case-list A21. Bulk work stopped at Reassign while `BulkTransitionDialog` and `BulkStatusTransitionService` already served the workflow board, so the four gestures a handler does most from a list were reachable only one case at a time. Each handler opens the SAME dialog in its own mode with a required reason: Suspend, Resume and Extend term are statutory acts (Awb 4:5 and 4:14) someone has to justify later, and doing twenty at once is exactly when the justification goes unwritten. The handlers are FUNCTIONS in src/customComponents.js, not the declarative `handler: "open-modal"` path: that path emits an `open-modal` event nothing in the library listens for, so declaring it would ship a bulk action that does nothing when clicked. Every icon here is registered in src/icons.js (hydra gate-60); a name that is not renders no icon at all rather than a fallback glyph.
config._teamColumnNote: `assignedGroup` is a $ref to an organisatieRol and CnIndexPage renders a plain key raw, so the column would show a uuid. `extend` asks OpenRegister to expand the reference on the fetch and the column reads the expanded row's `roleName`, the same shape the Tasks index uses for `case.title`; the server cannot sort on a nested field, so the column is not sortable. The Team FACET in the sidebar comes from `facetable: true` on the property itself, and lists-that-answer found that it is NOT the working interim this note used to claim. Two defects in the library, both outside dossiq and both one line. `useObjectStore` normalises a facet bucket as `{ value: b.key, count: b.count }`, but OpenRegister's bucket carries `results`, not `count`, so every option's count resolves to 0 and `CnIndexSidebar` renders it, because 0 is not undefined. The same normalisation drops `b.label`, and `getFilterOptions` renders `String(v.value)`, so a $ref facet lists uuids even on the fields where OpenRegister does resolve a name. The Team facet therefore reads as `<uuid> (0)` per team. The COLUMN is correct and is the real interim; the facet is a bug report. Do not cite it as coverage for the Team chip.
config._quickFiltersNote: one-case-list, D1 revised: the Queue page and the My Work page stay exactly as they are, and no menu entry changes. These chips only add the lenses to the list that already exists. Unclaimed carries the SAME two conditions as Queue's base filter (`assignee: "IS NULL"`, `isFinalStatus: false`), literally equal so the two lists cannot drift; the manifest vitest asserts that equality rather than trusting it. ALL IS THE DEFAULT, not Mine: `resolveInitialQuickFilterIndex` activates the chip marked `default` (and the FIRST chip when none is), so a Mine default would silently narrow every reader's first paint to their own cases and make an empty list look like an empty register. Ruben's revision to the change's own 'Mine is the default' decision; the same pattern parties-on-the-case established. Overdue spells its operator as the flat `deadline[lt]` key, not the nested `{ deadline: { lt } }` object: `buildQueryString` JSON-stringifies a nested object value, which reaches the API as the literal string `{"lt":"@today"}` and matches nothing. `@today` resolves client-side to `YYYY-MM-DD` at fetch time. Due this week (lists-that-answer) is the half-open window `[@today, @today+7d)`, written as TWO flat keys on the same field: OpenRegister's MagicSearchHandler reads `gte` and `lt` in separate `isset` branches and ANDs them, and PHP parses `deadline[gte]=` and `deadline[lt]=` into one nested array, so the pair survives the trip. `lt` rather than `lte` on the far edge, so a case due on day seven belongs to next week's chip and not to two chips at once. It carries no `statusHiddenInLists` of its own, matching its sibling Overdue rather than All.

columns.label: Requester
columns._note: contacts-domain 3.6. The requester is a person OR an organisation, and the two have separate detail pages, so the column needs a route chosen per row. `routeField` + `routeMap` on the built-in `link` cell widget (nextcloud-vue 2.47) read `initiatorType` off the row and pick the page; `params` maps the route's `:id` to the case's `requester` uuid. `contact` is deliberately absent from the map: a Nextcloud contact is not a register row and has no detail page here, so such a row falls back to plain text, which is what InitiatorSection.contactRouteBase() already returns null for. An app-side cell widget in src/cellWidgets.js could branch too, and was rejected: it would reimplement in dossiq the seam every fleet app needs.

columns.label: Status
columns._note: The Status column reads the status's own colour. `statusTypeName` alone resolves the $ref to a name and stops there, so five different statuses read as one grey column. A cell WIDGET rather than a second formatter, for the reason cellWidgets.js gives: a formatter returns a string and a string cannot carry a colour. The formatter stays as the fallback label the widget renders while the statusType collection is still loading.

columns.label: Deadline
columns._note: one-case-list A22. A raw ISO date makes every reader do the same subtraction once per row and get it wrong on the rows that matter. `deadlineCountdown` (src/services/cellWidgets.js) renders the days left and, past the deadline, the days overdue in the signalering red. A cell WIDGET rather than a `formatter` because a formatter returns a string and a string cannot carry the overdue state; nextcloud-vue 2.41 ships no built-in countdown cell, only `CnCountdownWidget` for a dashboard tile. The column stays sortable: CnDataTable sorts on the stored `deadline`, not on the rendered text.

config._transitionsNote: THE TRANSITION BUTTONS ARE GONE, AND MOVING THE CASE IS NOW A CLICK ON A STAGE. Ruben ruled on 2026-09-12: drop the transition strip and make clicking a status in the timeline widget set that status. So `actionsComponent` no longer names CaseTransitionsWidget, that component is deleted, and the `case-stages` widget carries the gesture. It is the same guarded move it always was, asked for in the same place it is shown: the widget reads OpenRegister /available-actions, dossiq answers that through CaseActionProvider off its own transition engine, and a stage no action reaches is disabled by construction rather than by a check somebody has to remember to write. The strip has been in three places now, and this is the reasoning that survived all three: the status belongs with the status, and the move belongs with the status too. Two things the strip carried have no home on this page any more, and they are named in the page `_note` rather than dropped in silence.
config._breadcrumbsNote: REMOVED, deliberately. The case page carried a trail whose LAST crumb was the case title, rendered one line below the page header that already printed that title: 'Cases > Dakkapel Kerkstraat 12' directly under 'Dakkapel Kerkstraat 12'. It read as a repeat rather than as a location, and it cost the top of the page a row. The way back to the list is the app menu, which is where the other detail pages in this app put it. This key stays as a note and not as config so the next reader finds out the trail was removed on purpose rather than re-adding it.
config._subtitleNote: Placement row A01: the case page did not say which case you are on. `identifier` is the case number, and it reads under the title. THE KEY IS INERT AND STAYS DECLARED ANYWAY. In @conduction/nextcloud-vue 2.49 `subtitleField` is read by CnObjectRow, CnIndexPage and CnObjectList and by no detail-page code at all, so deleting it would change nothing on screen and re-adding it later would look like a new idea. The number reads on the page because `case-tile-number` prints it, which is the same place CaseHeaderRow printed it.
config._note: CASE archetype (unified zaak) — the flagship record and the ADR-062 reference page (the cell is the budget: every widget fills its gridHeight exactly, no inner scrollbars, no reserved voids). The lead row pairs the field-scoped 'Core case data' widget (include: identity/ownership fields) with a right column of KPI stats-block (open tasks / documents / decisions / sub-cases, replacing the deprecated header summaryAggregates) over the Related panel. Row two pairs the 'Process' data widget (include: status/procedure/workflow fields) with Initiator, Contacts and Notes sized to their small content. FK-scoped child collections (task.case, caseDocument.case, decision.case, location.case) fit their rows to their cells with View-all/+N-more footers. Files and Calendar leaves close the page. THE TOP ROW IS FIVE CONFIGURED LIBRARY TILES AND NOTHING SPANS IT. It was one custom component, `case-header`, twelve columns wide and two rows tall, and Ruben's 2026-09-12 ruling is that the widgets on top of the page should be actual KPI widgets configured to show what they show, not a custom widget spanning an entire row. So the band is `case-tile-number`, `case-tile-type`, `case-tile-status`, `case-tile-assignee` and `case-tile-deadline`: four `stat` tiles and one `countdown` tile, all resolved by the library from `content`, none of them a registry component. The widths are 2, 3, 3, 2 and 2, because a case type title and a status name are phrases and a case number, a user id and a countdown are not. Under them the case's own progress is `case-stages`, the library `stages` widget, which is where the case is moved now. `lifecycleActions` is GONE -- it declared `{field: status}` and rendered nothing, because OpenRegister answers no actions for a $ref status field. Suspend, Resume, Extend term and Reopen are `open-modal` header actions onto one reason dialog (CaseLifecycleActionDialog), which reads /lifecycle before it posts. Only Reopen gates exactly as the spec words it, because `isFinalStatus` is on the case record: an action's local `visibleWhen` dot-paths into the loaded record, `suspensionAllowed` and `extensionAllowed` live on the case TYPE, and OpenRegister's object list IGNORES an `id` filter (it answers with the whole table), so a `source` predicate on the type would compare a different case type's flag and be wrong without saying so. Suspension is derived from the case's `activity` journal rather than a flag, so no field can gate Resume either, and that is the one thing this page lost when the transition strip went. The strip carried a Suspended marker and a second Resume button, both driven by GET /api/case/{id}/lifecycle. THE GESTURE STILL HAS A HOME: `case-resume` is a header action on this page and CaseLifecycleActionDialog reads /lifecycle before it posts, so a Resume on a case that is not suspended is refused with a sentence rather than silently accepted. THE MARKER DOES NOT. A `stat` tile's `overrides` test the LOADED RECORD, and no property of the case says it is suspended, so there is nothing for a configured tile to bind. Giving it one means materialising a suspension flag on the case, which is its own change: a flag written only on the next suspend would under-report every case suspended before it, and a wrong answer nobody can see is worse than a missing tile. Audit history IS the single sidebar history tab: the `version-history` tab is gone from this page (change case-stages, row A05), and the body strip carries no Timeline entry, so one log lives in one place. Copy case, Start and Plan follow-up (case-actions-menu, rows A24 to A26) are three more `open-modal` header actions, and NOT the `handler` type the design named: a handler action resolves `action.handler` against `effectiveManifest.actions`, which is a JSON map in this file and so cannot hold a function, and dossiq declares no such key, so the entry would warn to the console and do nothing when clicked. The id is `copy-case` and not `copy` because `copy` is one of the five reserved ids CnActionsBar drops at render time to avoid shadowing its built-in. None of the three passes props: open-modal forwards props verbatim without resolving tokens, so `@objectId` would arrive as that literal string, and each dialog reads the route instead. Start gates on `hasStartableFlows`, a materialised boolean on the CASE, exactly as `case-reopen` gates on `isFinalStatus` and for the same reason: a local visibleWhen dot-paths into the loaded case record, `startableFlows` lives on the case TYPE, and OpenRegister ignores an `id` filter so a `source` predicate on the type would compare a different case type's list and be wrong without saying so. An `endpoint` predicate cannot help either, because the URL is fetched verbatim with no token resolution and so cannot name this case.

widgets.title: Terms and payment
widgets._note: The statutory block: what the law gives you for this case, and what happens to the file afterwards. Every field here already existed on the schema and every one of them carried `visible: false`, which drops a property from every schema-driven surface at once, so the fields were declared and unreadable rather than merely unplaced. `statutoryTerm` is the type's processing deadline copied onto the case: the design asked for `extend` plus the include path `caseType.processingDeadline`, but a data widget builds its fields from the schema's OWN properties, so a dotted include matches nothing and renders nothing, and the stat-caption fallback interpolates only an endpoint payload. `hideEmpty` stays off on purpose: a case with no statutory term must show the row empty, because an absent term is itself the thing a handler is looking for. THE ARCHIVAL HALF MOVED OUT of this widget and no longer has a card of its own. `archiveNomination`, `archiveActionDate` and `archiveStatus` are still written on the case for its ZGW consumers, but they are read from `@self._retention`, the one place any app can ask an object what happens to it and when, and they surface in the object metadata panel under its Archiving category alongside every other `@self` fact. A data widget cannot bind that, because it builds its fields from the schema's own properties and reads them off the top level of the record. The separate `case-archival` card that briefly held them is gone: it duplicated a category the metadata panel already groups, and it spent five rows of the right column saying what the panel says in five.

widgets.title: Hours booked
widgets._note: Hours live in humaniq, per ADR-107 decision 6: 'Hours logged on a case are hrmq time entries carrying the case reference.' So humaniq renders them. This widget is a PLACEMENT of humaniq's `humaniq-hours` leaf, not a query against another app's register. It used to be a stats-block that summed `humaniq`/`TimeEntry` straight out of this manifest, filtered on `domainObjectType` and `domainObjectRef`. On an install without humaniq that endpoint 404s and the tile renders `0`, which is exactly what a case with no hours booked renders: no error, no empty state, nothing a reader would notice. ADR-113 names that class. A leaf whose app is absent is never registered, so the surface goes missing rather than lying. The leaf identifies the host object the way humaniq stores it: `domainObjectType` is the `<app>:<schema>` literal and `domainObjectRef` is the object uuid. Nothing here declares either one. The host forwards `register`, `schema` and `objectId` to every leaf it mounts, and this page's config carries `dossiq` and `case`, so the literal comes out `dossiq:case`. `requiredApp: humaniq` went with the query. It was the honest form of the tile while the tile still read another app's register, and no other integration widget in this manifest declares one. The `log-hours` header action went with it. It wrote a TimeEntry through `open-form`, which the leaf's own Book hours dialog now does, seeded from the same object and beside the total those hours land in. Two booking paths on one page is one more than a reader needs, and the header one was the further from the figure it changes.

widgets.title: Flow runs
widgets._note: case-flow-human-steps 6.1, the case half: this case's own flow run and the step it sits on, with its finished runs underneath (nextcloud-vue CnFlowRunsWidget in subject mode). `subject: '@objectId'` binds the current case, so OpenRegister filters the active and completed reads to it server-side. `rowRoute` and not `runRoute` on purpose: dossiq has no run detail page, and FlowDetail (/flows/:id) resolves a FLOW id, so a click opens the flow. Pointing runRoute at FlowDetail would push a run uuid into a flow route and open nothing. The row click also carries the clicked run as `?run=`, so FlowDetail opens with that run inspected and the canvas showing the graph version the run actually executed, rather than the flow's current graph with no run selected. Nothing here declares that: the widget adds the query, and CnPageRenderer forwards `run` to a flow page because that page type declares it reads it.

content.subject: @objectId
content.emptyText: No flow is running for this case

widgets.title: Case number
widgets._note: Placement row A01, first tile, and the one that answers REQ-CDV-14 in practice. The requirement asks for the case number to read under the title through `config.subtitleField`, and the manifest sets it, but nothing on a detail page consumes it: in @conduction/nextcloud-vue 2.49 `subtitleField` is read by CnObjectRow, CnIndexPage and CnObjectList and by no detail-page code at all. So the key stays declared for the day it lands, and the number is a tile in the meantime, which is the same place CaseHeaderRow printed it. `objectField` in its plain string form: `identifier` is generated by OpenRegister and stored on the case, so there is nothing to look up. ⚠️ A `stat` tile FORMATS ITS VALUE AS A NUMBER when the value parses as one, and the library offers no text style to turn that off. The generated number is YEAR-NNNN, which never parses, so it prints as stored; an imported case that kept a bare digit string for a number would come out with thousands separators. Small, and named here rather than worked around with a prefix that would then show on every case.

content.label: Case number
content.emptyText: Not issued

widgets.title: Case type
widgets._note: Placement row A01, second tile. A CONFIGURED library `stat` tile, not a hand-written component: `objectField` holds the case's `caseType` uuid and `resolve` looks the row up in the dossiq register and reads its `title`, which is the uuid-to-title resolve the retired `case-kpi-casetype` tile and then CaseHeaderRow both carried in JavaScript. `emptyText` reads Not set for a case whose type cannot be read, so an unresolvable reference never prints a raw uuid at a reader: a uuid under the title is a fact about the database, not about the case. The tile takes three of twelve columns. Ruben's ruling on 2026-09-12 is that the top of this page is KPI widgets configured to show what they show, and that none of them spans a row, so the one full-width custom band that used to sit here is five tiles now.

content.label: Case type
content.emptyText: Not set

widgets.title: Deadline
widgets._note: Placement row A01, fifth tile. The library `countdown` widget TYPE, and deliberately not `stat` with `display: countdown`, which 2.50 also offers and which would make the row five tiles of one type. Three reasons, and the first is the one that decided it. THE WORDINGS WOULD LAND ON THE WRONG CATALOGUE. `CnStatWidget` runs every string through the host's translate function, which this app binds to `ncT('dossiq', key)` in App.vue, so `1 day left`, `{n} days left`, `Today` and `Overdue by {n} days` would become dossiq strings that no gate checks: gate 102 reads manifest strings only, and `check:l10n-js` compares nl.json to nl.js, so a string missing from both is reported in sync. They would render English to a Dutch user and nothing would say so. The `countdown` widget translates them against nextcloud-vue's own catalogue instead, with nothing for this app to maintain. Second, it keeps the absolute date under the headline, which `caption` cannot carry because caption tokens interpolate only from an endpoint payload and this tile is in record mode. Third, configuring `futureLabel` and `pastLabel` to dodge the first reason costs the singular: a configured template replaces both forms, so a case one day out would read `1 days left`. The consistency given up is a type name and a prop name rather than anything a reader sees, because both renderers emit the same `cn-kpi-card` markup from the same stylesheet. It reads a date off the loaded record and does the arithmetic without a request. `thresholds` are the `warn 14, danger 5` bands the retired Time left tile counted with and CaseHeaderRow carried after it: they follow the handling rhythm rather than round numbers, because at two weeks a handler still has room to act and at five days they do not. A date in the past reads as overdue rather than as a negative number, and a case with no deadline reads as a dash in no threshold colour, because a case that has claimed no deadline is neither urgent nor on time. `showDate` keeps the absolute date under the headline: how long and when are two questions and a handler asks both.

widgets.title: Timeline
widgets._note: The case's own progress, as the library `stages` widget: placeable, configurable, and the thing a handler clicks to move the case. The id is `case-stages` and NOT `case-timeline`, which is reserved: `tests/vitest/manifestCaseTimeline.spec.js` asserts this page declares no widget by that id, because row A05 keeps one history in one place and a body panel over the audit log beside the sidebar History tab would be two views of one log. This widget is not that log. It is where the case is in its process and where it is moved. It replaces the custom CaseStepsWidget, whose note said a `stepper` widget type over a reference field's ordered sibling rows would make this a config declaration and that until nextcloud-vue shipped one the custom widget was the interim. It shipped, and this is the declaration. `stagesEndpoint` reads the case type's BLUEPRINT rather than its own statusType rows: a type that derives its lifecycle from a parent has none of its own, so the plain query said this case type has no statuses about a case type that plainly has four, and /blueprint merges the chain server-side. `@object.caseType` is resolved against the loaded case by the library's shared token grammar, and a token that resolves empty blocks the request instead of fetching a url with a hole in it. `transition: {kind: lifecycle}` is what makes a stage clickable: the widget reads OpenRegister's /available-actions, which dossiq answers through CaseActionProvider off its own transition engine, and posts to /transition. 🔴 THE POST IS REFUSED TODAY, AND NOT BY THIS APP. OpenRegister's provider mode is read-only: `deriveActions()` asks the provider, `applyTransition()` has no provider branch, and `LifecycleActionProviderInterface` declares no `execute()`, so a POST of an action the provider itself published comes back `Transition <action> is not declared on this schema.` and the case stays where it is. openregister#3679. `{kind: field}` is NOT the answer: it writes `status` with nothing validating the move, so a handler could close a case with no result and no guard check, and the whole point of this binding is that OpenRegister re-validates. The declaration stays as it is and this page waits for the write half. A stage no action reaches is disabled with the configured `unreachableReason`, and a stage whose move the engine REFUSES is disabled with the guard's own sentence: CaseActionProvider publishes a refused move with `blocked: true` and the guard's `failureMessage` as its description, and 2.50's `stageAccess()` reads that flag. So the refusal is drawn before the click rather than met after it, and `onStageClick` refuses a blocked move as well, so no path through the widget posts one. Both kinds of refusal fail closed twice over, because OpenRegister still re-validates the POST through the same engine that published the verdict. Vertical: a status name is a phrase, not a word, and laid out left to right those phrases wrap into stacked columns that read as a table rather than as a sequence.

It was keyed on `schemaSlug: caseTask` and fed OpenRegister's schema-scoped unified search only, so with no objects of that schema it matched nothing and resolved nothing. Engine tasks therefore have NO unified-search provider today. That gap is OpenRegister's: the engine's tasks live in their own table and no deep-link shape addresses them, and a dossiq entry cannot invent one. config._note: CASE-TYPE / WORKFLOW-DEFINITION archetype (the state machine that drives cases of a caseType), ADR-062 round 2. No comms. Cases driven by this workflow are reached through their caseType index rather than a direct FK (case.workflowTemplate stores a version reference, not this object's id), so no object-list is scoped here. Publish/Deprecate/Clone admin actions are preserved as page actions and lifecycleActions drive the lifecycleStatus. Audit history (version changes) is a sidebar tab.

TRANSITION-RECORD archetype (an immutable entry for one case status transition). No comms/documents and it is itself a history entry, so it stays lean. The Data widget shows the transition and its side-effects (case, fromStatus→statusType, transitionLabel, noWorkflowTemplate, the evaluatedGuards[] that were checked and the dispatchedActions[] that fired); a Related panel links the parent case. No lifecycleActions — a status record is a frozen fact, not a mutable object. No content leaves. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

ASSESSMENT-RECORD archetype (a per-case LHS intervention recommendation derived from an lhsMatrix), ADR-062 round 2. No comms/documents, no child schemas. The 13-field schema splits into two genuinely distinct groups: 'Recommendation' (the matrix inputs and outcome — case, inspection, ernst, gedrag, actorType, matrixVersion, recommendedInterventie, recommendedBy) paired with the Related panel (parent case and inspection), and 'Override & final' (the accountability-bearing deviation fields — finalIntervention, override, overrideJustification, overrideBy, overrideAuthority) full-width below. No status lifecycle field and no content leaves. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

COMMITTEE archetype (bezwaaradviescommissie / BAC), ADR-062 round 2. No comms leaves on the schema. A committee is defined by its constitution and its caseload; the schema splits into two genuinely distinct groups: 'Committee' (name, type, domain, jurisdiction, quorum, active — the constitution) and 'Roster & term' (chair, secretary, members[], termStartsOn, termEndsOn, created — who sits and until when). The lead row pairs the constitution widget with an in-grid KPI stats-block (total assignments + in-deliberation workload via bacAdviceRequest.status, replacing the deprecated header summaryAggregates). Below: the roster widget full-width, then the advice-assignment object-list (bacAdviceRequest.commissie=@objectId). No status lifecycle (active is a boolean). Audit history (composition/term changes) is a sidebar tab.

pages.title: Case types

config._formNote: The Add dialog on this page asked all 41 of caseType's properties, in one column, at default dialog width. Nothing was wrong with the dialog: CnFormDialog has taken `size` and `columns` since two-column forms shipped, but CnIndexPage passed neither, so the built-in Add form had no way to ask. The `case` create form on the Dashboard and the two contact pages is two columns already because it is an `open-form` HEADER ACTION, and CnActionButtons did forward both keys. Same app, same kind of record, two different forms, and no manifest key that explained the difference. nextcloud-vue 2.46.0 adds `formSize`/`formColumns` to CnIndexPage, CnDetailPage, CnObjectListWidget and CnObjectDataWidget, which is what these two keys reach.
config._includeFieldsNote: Twelve of the forty-one, and every one of them is also on CaseTypeDetail, so nothing here becomes unreachable by being left off the create form. The cut follows the detail page's own grouping: this is `case-type-core` (title, identifier, description, category, parentCaseType, purpose, trigger, handlingModel, confidentiality, isDraft) plus the two facts from `case-type-terms` that a type cannot sensibly start life without, its statutory `processingDeadline` and the `validFrom` it takes effect on. What is deliberately NOT here: the versioning trio (version, previousVersion, supersededBy) is written by the publish action, not typed; the relation lists (subCaseTypes, decisionTypes, relatedCaseTypes, startableFlows) are built up on the detail page once the thing they point at exists; the AVG block (case-type-privacy) is a data protection officer's pass over an existing type rather than an author's first screen; and the remaining specialist codings (layerIds, iv3TaskField, selectionListProcessType, referenceProcess, verwerkingsactiviteit) are lookups nobody has to hand while naming a new type. `initialStatus` is excluded for a HARDER reason, the same one the CaseTypes-adjacent `case` form records for `status`: it is a $ref to a statusType filtered by `caseType`, and at create time this case type has no id and therefore no statuses, so the picker would fetch unfiltered and offer every OTHER type's statuses. Half of those are called `Received` or `In progress`, which makes them both indistinguishable and wrong. A type's statuses are authored on its detail page, after it exists.
config._fieldOverridesNote: `order` is set here rather than on the register because fieldsFromSchema resolves an override's `order` AHEAD of the property's own, so one manifest map orders every schema-driven surface without a data-model change. It is not cosmetic: not one of caseType's 41 properties carries an `order`, so the sort falls through to alphabetical and a form that opens on `Category` puts `Title` TENTH. The three prose fields are declared `textarea` because caseType leaves them as plain strings with no maxLength, so resolveWidget renders a single-line input for what is a paragraph. That also decides the layout: CnFormDialog spans a textarea across BOTH columns (WIDE_WIDGETS), so the nine single-line fields pair up into rows first and the three prose fields follow full width, which is why the order puts them last. Interleaved, each one would leave the column beside it empty.
config._folderSidebarNote: `source: "field"` and not `source: "facet"`. CnIndexPage still resolves exactly four sources, register, field, custom and files, and CnFolderSidebar's own validator takes only custom, field and files, so a sidebar declared as a facet falls through to `custom`, finds the (absent) `folders` array and renders an empty pane. THE SECOND HALF OF THIS NOTE WAS TRUE UNTIL nextcloud-vue 2.42.0 AND IS NOT ANY MORE: `field` no longer derives the folders from the distinct `category` values of the loaded rows. Since #1036 it prefers the FACET for `field`, which is computed over the whole query with pagination stripped, and only groups the rows when no facet arrives. That is what makes a category reachable when every row carrying it sits on a later page, and it is why no manifest change is wanted here: `facetable: true` on the property plus `source: "field"` is the whole contract, and the object store adds `_facets=extend` on its own once the fetched schema has any facetable property. `x-openregister-facet` is still read by nothing. ⚠️ The facet ARRIVES an hour stale, because OpenRegister caches the response and no object write invalidates it, so a category added today gets no folder today: OpenRegister#3560, and the reason the folder e2e test is parked.

pages._note: A case type is the blueprint every case is governed by — lifecycle, deadlines, classification, the workflow that drives it — and `case.caseType` references it. It had no surface at all: the original `CaseTypesMenu` pointed at the in-app `/settings` page, which page-topology-cleanup B1 retired for mounting AdminRoot through the in-app router (ADR-004), and no replacement was ever built. The capability went with the page and only its stale `settingsSection` id was left behind. WorkflowDefinitionDetail's own note still says cases are 'reached through their caseType index', naming this page. Restored as an ordinary schema-driven index rather than by reviving the retired settings route.

widgets.title: Versions

widgets.title: Statuses, results and attributes
widgets._note: The one widget on this page that a declared type cannot be. An object-list fetches OpenRegister itself, so the only question it can ask is `statusType where caseType = @objectId` -- the type's OWN rows. A type that derives its lifecycle from a parent has none of those, so three declared lists would render three empty tables about a case type that plainly has four statuses, and nothing would say so. The merge exists only in CaseTypeResolver, and /api/case-types/{id}/blueprint is how a page reads it. It sits in the LAYOUT and not inside a tab strip on purpose: a `type: "custom"` widget named as a tab CHILD resolves by registry TYPE, finds nothing, and renders an empty panel without logging anything.

config._headerActionsNote: There is no `run-action` header-action type. The manifest schema enumerates handler, open-modal, open-page, navigate, object-op, export, open-form, refresh, api-call, agent and toggle, and CnActionButtons resolves exactly those; the design's `run-action` would have been refused by `npm run check:manifest` and, had it slipped through, rendered a button that dispatches nothing. Export is an `api-call` with `download: true`, which is the shape that asks for the response as a blob and hands it to the browser -- the endpoint already answers a DataDownloadResponse. The other three are dialogs, each for a reason a declarative action cannot meet: Import takes a FILE (a confirm gate has no fields and an api-call sends JSON), Publish must show the validation findings BEFORE asking for a change note, and Duplicate must land on the copy rather than refresh the page you are already on. Every icon here is registered in src/icons.js (gate-60); a name that is not renders no icon at all. The three dialogs read the case type off the ROUTE and not off their props: `open-modal` forwards props verbatim, so a `@objectId` token would arrive as that literal string.

NO TAB STRIP: `case-type-one-authoring-surface` owns that, and building one here would be the second strip the moment it lands. These are layout cells, and they become that strip's children when it arrives -- except `case-type-blueprint`, which cannot be a tab child while it is `type: "custom"`.

pages.title: Store
pages._note: ADR-080: the store plane. Discovery belongs to OpenRegister — this page reads /api/store/items, which is a thin action over AppHost's GenericStoreService, so the SSRF guard, the redirect refusal and the token live in the engine and dossiq builds no registry URL. A custom component rather than type:index because store items are REMOTE objects: the object-backed index renderer resolves a local register+schema and cannot address them. With no registry configured the engine answers not_configured WITHOUT a network call and the page renders dossiq's built-in templates, which is Decision 4 and the only reason this surface may carry the word Store at all. Install is dossiq's own and admin-guarded (Decision 3), and it writes case CONFIGURATION only — the record schemas are refused. PLACEMENT: footer, order 92, between Documentation (90) and Reports (95). openbuild, hermiq and integriq put Store in the main section instead; ADR-080 records no placement decision, so one of the two conventions is wrong and the ADR needs an amendment either way.

pages.title: Flows
pages._note: ADR-110 Decision 4: a flow is app-specific — a dossiq flow operates on cases — so the authoring surface lives here rather than behind a deep link to OpenRegister's list. An ordinary index over the NAMED flows source: a flow lives in the shared native flow store, not a register/schema, so the object-backed index cannot address it. Scoped app="dossiq" — the same store OpenRegister, integriq and hermiq use, so list/status semantics stay identical fleet-wide. rowRoute names the FlowDetail page (a route NAME, not a path): a named-source page has no register+schema, so CnPageRenderer cannot infer a detail page, and without an explicit target the row click and the Edit action fall back to the source's /flows path rather than the page this manifest declares. Mirrors openregister/src/manifest.json:flows.

pages.title: Flow
pages._note: The shared CnFlowDetail node/edge canvas over the same native flow store OpenRegister and hermiq use — not an app-owned editor. Controls live in the NcAppSidebar (sidebarComponent) so the canvas gets full width; canvas and sidebar share useFlowStore. Mirrors openregister/src/manifest.json:flowDetail.

config._typeNote: The change's design (D2) asked for `type: "settings"`. The installed @conduction/nextcloud-vue dist cannot host this page there, and the reason is worth writing down rather than rediscovering. A `settings` section's `widgets[]` resolves ONLY against BUILTIN_SETTINGS_WIDGETS (`version-info`, `register-mapping`) and the `component` discriminator; `object-list` is a DASHBOARD widget (`registerDashboardWidget('object-list', …)`), so it would resolve to nothing, log one console warn and render an empty section. CnSettingsPage also takes no page-level `widgets[]` prop, so the uniform grid is not a way in either. Task 2.2 named this exact outcome and the interim it licenses: an `index` page over the config schema, never a `custom` page (the ADR-100 ratchet). The cost is REQ-ADMIN-021 — the Required apps section, which needs `CnLeafDependencySettings` through a `type: "component"` widget — and that requirement stays red until a settings section can host a list. Nothing here needs to change when it can: the columns and the seed are the page.
config._openSettingsNote: Open settings is a COLUMN with the built-in `link` widget, not a row action, because a row action cannot carry a per-row URL or a per-row visibility. `type: "navigate"` takes one literal `target` for the whole column and pushes it through vue-router, which cannot reach /settings/admin/dossiq at all; `handler` reaches the row but CnRowActions' `visible` predicate is a FUNCTION, which JSON cannot carry, and the action schema is additionalProperties:false so the key would be rejected anyway. The `link` widget substitutes `{settingsUrl}` from the row and, when that resolves to the empty string, `linkHref` is falsy and the cell falls through to plain text — which is exactly what REQ-ADMIN-019 asks for on the BRP and KvK rows: no Open settings offered.

pages.title: Contacts

config._folderSidebarNote: THE FOLDER SIDEBAR IS STILL ABSENT, AND IT IS NO LONGER WAITED ON. `contacts-domain` recorded why one could not ship, and both measurements still hold against nextcloud-vue 2.41.0. FIRST, there is no `hidden`: `folderSidebarFolders()` hands `folders[]` to CnFolderTree verbatim, so an Organisations folder would render, and selecting it would filter this page's `brpPerson` rows by a value no person carries and show an empty list. SECOND, `filterField: "@self.schema"` is not a filter OpenRegister answers: the wire form is a NESTED `@self` object (see `VthSeedLookup`'s `['@self' => ['slug' => ...]]`), so a flat `@self.schema` key reads as a filter on a field no object has and the search returns nothing while looking like an empty register. WHAT CHANGED is the question the sidebar was answering. It was never wanted for its own sake; it was the only way anyone could think of to reach the ten `kvkCompany` rows, which until now were listed on no page at all. The `Organisations` page below is that list, as a CHILD of this entry, so the answer costs no top-level navigation and no folder seam. If B10 ever lands, a folder that swaps the schema becomes a presentation choice between two pages rather than the thing that decides whether organisations are reachable, which is the right size for it.

The address column reads `residence.city` rather than a composed address line: a column key IS a dot-path into the row (CnDataTable.getCellValue splits on `.`), and there is no composed address field to read. It is `sortable: false` on purpose — the dot-path resolves for RENDERING, off the row the page already holds, but a sort sends the key to OpenRegister as an `_order` field, and the same dot-path that reads an inline object client-side is not a column the server can order by.

observability._note: Declarative observability via OpenRegister's AppHost engine (ADR-040). Reproduces the output of the now-deleted hand-written HealthController + MetricsController. The /api/health and /api/metrics routes are aliased to AppHost\Controller\GenericHealth#index / GenericMetrics#index, so the engine reads this block at request time. Parity: metric names (with the engine-added dossiq_ prefix), types, HELP texts and label keys (incl. the caseType JSON field surfacing as the case_type label) match the pre-adoption contract; the implicit dossiq_info / dossiq_up gauges are emitted by the engine. The APCu controller-local cache is replaced by the engine's per-metric cacheTtl via the distributed cache (same 30s/60s TTLs, shared across workers). 🔴 `dossiq_tasks_total` AND `dossiq_tasks_overdue_total` ARE GONE, and they are the one break in that parity. Both were `kind: objectCount` over `schema: caseTask`, and remove-casetask deleted the schema: a counter over a schema nothing declares reports 0 for ever, which on a task gauge reads as a quiet week rather than as a broken metric. Task counts belong to whoever owns the tasks, and that is now OpenRegister's task engine, which is exporting them itself in openregister#3597. An `objectCount` source cannot reach the engine's table, so there is nothing dossiq can declare here in the meantime.
